To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the three-dimensional structure of herpes simplex virus is asymmetric; that the tegument forms an asymmetric cap around the capsid; that the teguments substructure is particulate with some short actinic-like filaments; and that the envelope contains 600-750 glycoprotein spike that vary in length, spacing and in the angles that they emerge from the envelope.

cryo–electron microscopy and tomography of herpes simplex virus revealed that the tegument is a complex structure that surrounds the nucleocapsid, that the capsid is separated from the envelope by a layer of tegument, that the tegument contains short actin-like fibers, and that the envelope contains glycoprotein spikes in a nonrandom arrangement.
herpes simplex virus is an asymmetric, complex virion, and the tegument and the envelope are highly pleomorphic.

the three-dimensional structure of herpes simplex virus (HSV) and other viruses.
the structure and function of the herpes virus tegument and envelope.
understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying the replication of herpesviruses and the development of antiviral drugs that interfere with this process.

herpes simplex virus is an asymmetric capsid with an asymmetric tegument and an asymmetric envelope.
the herpes virus is an asymmetric capsid surrounded by an irregularly shaped tegument and an envelope containing an unusual array of spikes.

the structure of the tegument and envelope is not uniform, but instead is highly complex.
